title: Am making an vibe coded soccer game what would you like to be on it
author: newaccmeee
selftext:
As in title, am trying to build a videogame, so far am borrowing heavily from both FIFA and PES games all the way from FIFA 19 and 23 as well PES 13 18 19, so far the game is progressing far from finished, did make a polygon prototype and it runs well built on python but things like game physics or ball physics or crowd and commentary are too arcadic and to build one from scratch and be playable not like the prototype is near impossible since no real engine is open source and helpful.

To make it flavourful i was think the game could be based on an old world cup, something in the 90s and 80s and now am building the mesh of kits back then to not look like modern polyester shirts so the heavy cotton kits and the short shorts. I haven't seen anyone do a full on playable soccer game vibe coded so far been so locked in it felt like am th one building it, it's being taught on frequent testings and motion of real clips from youtube. Should I break all licenses and add actual logos and stuff on it ? Would you play it if it does make a launch and what feature do you like you wanna add ?

If it does become possible a career mode where selecting sponsors tv rights and match tickets and all contribute to transfer budgets is cool, I wanna add realism for it to not be FIFA arcadic but not gta6 realistic.

Lmk

comments.author: New_Internal5636
comments.body:
Football games are very complicated to build hence why companies trying to make rival games to FIFA and efootball have pretty much all failed. They've built somewhat working adequate working football games yes but the issue more is balancing and tuning a football game that people like and enjoy. Getting the mechanics to be balanced and pacing to be faster (since no one wants to play real life paced football, pretty much every football game is 20x the speed of real football) is something not even the games like FIFA and PES have really mastered. Well I enjoy these games but they are far from perfect and I've sorted of realised that they likely never will be. 

People think just make it realistic but that's actually way more complex than you think. Realistic football in most cases does not make for a good video game experience so you have to tweak it in some way or another to be video game suitable. 

So I would recommend going for something very much simplified unless you plan on never finishing it. There is a reason why this hasn't been done and likely will not be attempted much other than by people with much larger development budgets. Try something totally unique I say if you actually want it to go somewhere.
